extracted.intended_audience: CBC Radio listeners and general public interested in India, religion, free speech, and current affairs
extracted.subtask_description: A news report about an Indian Muslim comedian arrested under Section 295A for allegedly insulting religion, summarizing the incident, legal basis for the charge, political context, and possible penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 295A of India's penal code
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 295A of India's penal code prohibits "deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article illustrates enforcement of this provision: Munawar Faruqui was arrested under Section 295A after a Hindu group disrupted his show. Police and officials have said there is "enough evidence," and an officer noted Faruqui "was going to" make jokes that allegedly would have insulted religion — indicating authorities may act on anticipated or planned remarks as well as published content. The complainant named is Eklavya Singh Gaur, convenor of the disrupting group; multiple people connected to the event were arrested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegations for insulting deities / incitement (Uttar Pradesh case)
rubrics_metrics.description: Faruqui is also facing charges in Uttar Pradesh state for a comedy video in which he allegedly insulted Hindu deities and implies that Home Minister Amit Shah incited violence against Muslims, according to Al Jazeera.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior recordings or videos that are interpreted as insulting religious figures or as alleging incitement by political leaders can form the basis for separate criminal complaints. The article uses this as an example of how past material can be relied upon in different jurisdictions (Uttar Pradesh) to bring charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties, detention, and bail outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: If convicted, Faruqui could face up to four years imprisonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece notes Faruqui was detained for more than three weeks and that his bail applications have been rejected; it also emphasizes claims by his lawyer and manager that the detention is politically motivated or "just harassment," and that the legal process may take months. This indicates both the potential sentence severity and the practical realities (detention length, bail denials) surrounding such charges.
